subject: Workplace Skills
title: Perfectionism as Procrastination
description: A short lesson to help you apply Perfectionism as Procrastination.

hook.text: Voltaire wrote that the perfect is the enemy of the good. 300 years later the insight still cuts deep.

buildup.text: Perfectionism disguises itself as high standards. In practice it delays shipping and prevents feedback.

discovery.text: The 80% version released today generates real data. The 100% version that never ships generates nothing.

twist.text: Perfectionists polish what doesn't need polishing. The market rarely notices the last 20% you agonized over.

climax.text: Set a 'good enough' threshold before starting. When you hit it, ship. Refine only if data demands it.

punchline.text: Ship at good enough. Perfect never arrives.

quiz.question: Why is perfectionism often counterproductive?
options: It always results in lower quality work
It delays delivery and prevents getting real feedback
